note:
GHOST VALUES -- example arguments, keyed by PARAMETER NAME then by TYPE. Merged into Deploy/OURONET-REGISTRY.json by REPL/tools/_registry.py; that file is generated and this one is not, so regenerating can never destroy these.

TWO USE TAGS -- `zbom` and `tooltip` (owner ruling, 2026-09-27). A ghost value is not equally safe on every surface, and until now one value served both. `zbom` = may be PREFILLED into a ZBOM input, i.e. it can end up in a signed transaction. `tooltip` = may be RENDERED in a pre-ZBOM tooltip, where nothing is ever submitted. Both default to TRUE when absent, so every existing entry keeps its behaviour.

The case that forced it is `guard`. A guard cannot be prefilled -- nobody may hand a user a keyset to sign under -- so `zbom` is false. But a tooltip that shows the guard slot EMPTY teaches the wrong call shape, so `tooltip` is true with a `display` override rendering the Pact form the caller actually writes. That is a value which is correct to show and wrong to submit, which is precisely the distinction one tag cannot carry.

`display` is an optional RENDER override for tooltips. Absent, the tooltip renders `v`. Present, it renders `display` -- used where the submittable form and the readable form differ.

WHY SOME NAMES STILL HAVE NO ENTRY, and that is deliberate. A parameter with no byParam and no byType match falls through to the generic `"example"`, which a consumer renders as a visible placeholder. That is the CORRECT outcome for an entity that does not exist on mainnet -- zero anchors, zero scores -- and for one whose real id nobody here can cite. Fabricating a plausible-looking id would remove the only signal that the slot is unresolved, and a confident wrong id is worse than an obvious gap: it gets copied, and it makes a preview SUCCEED against the wrong entity. Entries are added only when the value can be cited.

OBJECT-TYPED ENTRIES, added 2026-10-29, and they are why seven vacate buttons and four wipe buttons had no renderable preview. A PREVIEW'S PARAMETER LIST IS NOT THE EXECUTION'S: CCp_BatchVacateTrueFungible takes three parallel arrays while its INFO_ takes one `legs:[object{VCT|VacateTfLeg}]`, so the entrypoint's own composed ghost has nothing under that name and the lookup falls through to this table. With no entry here, OuronetUI's generate-execution-specs.py filed the op in SPEC_SKIPPED -- and a button whose preview cannot render is a button wired without the evidence that it is wired correctly, which is the one thing the preview exists to supply.

THE FIELD NAMES ARE CHECKED, because nothing else here checks them. `ghost_fits` validates an object ghost only as far as `isinstance(v, dict)`, so a renamed schema field would leave a silently stale example that renders fine and then fails on chain. `_ghostshape.py --check` (fatal in the gate) compares every object-typed entry in this table against the defschema its type names, field for field and type for type.

string.why: fallback only -- a string parameter with no name entry above

guard.why:
a guard is passed as `(read-keyset "ks")` -- this is the NAME of the transaction-data key, not the keyset. Put {"keys": [...], "pred": "keys-all"} in the transaction's `data` under that name. Inlining the keyset object is not a thing Pact accepts.
zbom:false -- a ZBOM must make the user supply their own keyset. Prefilling a guard is handing someone a lock and asking them to sign for it. tooltip:true because a tooltip submits nothing, and an empty guard slot teaches the wrong call shape.

object.why: UNTYPED in the signature, so there is no schema to derive a shape from. Read the entrypoint's @doc -- an empty object here means 'the contract did not say', not 'send nothing'.

[object].why: untyped list-of-object; see the note on `object`.

[[string]].why: A list OF LISTS, for the bulk-transfer fan-out where one token's recipients are an inner list. One outer entry with one inner entry: the shape is what has to be right, not the length. It is positional against transfer-amount-array, so a preview rendered two-deep here and one-deep there would price a call the contract refuses.

[[decimal]].why: The amount side of the same fan-out, kept in lockstep with [[string]] above at one outer entry each.

[object{AcquisitionSchemasV3.VCT|VacateT.why: ONE vacate leg for a DPTF asset: who gets custody back, who was earning on it, how much. Fields and types are AQP's own VCT|VacateTfLeg -- `balance` is a decimal, and a bare 1 in that slot does not coerce in Pact.

[object{AcquisitionSchemasV3.VCT|VacateN.why: The nonce-bearing counterpart, used by every ortofungible and collectable vacate preview. `nonces` and `amounts` are POSITIONAL against each other INSIDE the leg -- one entry each, because a mismatched pair is the silent failure this shape exists to make visible.

[object{AcquisitionSchemasV3.VCT|VacateT.why: One DPTF asset-lane of a whole-pool vacate: the asset plus its legs. This is the PHASE-1 scan's output shape, so a preview rendered from it is rendered from the same thing the execution is fed.

[object{AcquisitionSchemasV3.VCT|VacateN.why: The nonce-bearing lane, used TWICE by the whole-pool vacate preview -- once for ortofungible satellites and once for collectables. Same schema both times, which is why one entry serves.

object{DpofUdcV2.RemovableNonces}.why: The ortofungible wipe's preflight bundle. SEPARATE FROM THE DPDC ONE BELOW AND NOT INTERCHANGEABLE: both schemas are named RemovableNonces, and this one's `r-amounts` is [decimal] while DPDC's is [integer]. Sharing a value between them would render a decimal into an integer slot, which Pact refuses -- the same two-schemas-one-name hazard the registry's partition note already records for URHC_WipePure.

object{DpdcManagementV3.RemovableNonces}.why: The collectable (DPSF/DPNF) wipe's preflight bundle. `r-amounts` is [integer] here, not [decimal] -- see the DPOF entry above for why these two cannot share a value.
